identityReviewRetry.reason: First identity correction retained a swept-up crown and generic beard instead of the native tight curl cap and lower-lip bare gaps.
identityReviewRetry.observedSource: The native hair is cropped almost to the scalp into tiny densely packed curls, with no quiff or raised front wave, leaving a high open forehead. Short beard has bare skin patches beside a central sublip tuft.
identityReviewRetry.observedResult: The first retry still has a longer wavy combed-up front ridge and a uniformly groomed beard; it remains too close to the other generated Imperial men.
identityReviewRetry.correction: Apply the previous full modifiers and identity correction. Give this particular man a close buzz-cut silhouette with tiny dark chestnut coiled hair texture, uniformly scalp-hugging over top and sides. The hair length is about 3 millimeters, so individual locks cannot sweep upward or backward and there is no quiff, crest, fringe, pompadour or raised frontal wave. Keep the entire high broad forehead open. This is the visible native very short curl-cap hairstyle, not baldness. Maintain the native elongated ordinary oval face, muted green almond eyes and fine brows. Preserve the short shaped beard with a separate central sublip tuft bordered immediately on both sides by clearly visible small bare skin patches before the beard resumes along the chin. Keep natural reddish cheeks and ordinary facial asymmetry. Do not add scars, tattoos or distinguishing features.
